condition: Colorectal cancer screening — average risk, age 45–49
permutationLabel: Average risk, age 46 (base case for the screening cluster)
summary: 46-year-old asymptomatic woman at a wellness visit asks about bowel cancer screening; no family history, never screened. USPSTF 2021 starts average-risk screening at 45 (FIT yearly or colonoscopy 10-yearly).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Wellness check — asking about bowel cancer screening
inputs.hpi: Well 46-year-old woman attending for a wellness check. Asks whether she should have bowel cancer screening after a colleague was diagnosed. No change in bowel habit, no rectal bleeding, no weight loss, no abdominal pain. Never had a colonoscopy or stool test. No family history of bowel cancer or polyps.
inputs.socialHistory: Bank officer. Never smoked. Alcohol 2–3 units/week.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Colorectal cancer screening — average risk, age 46
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic, average risk, age 46. Colorectal cancer screening discussion: annual FIT or colonoscopy every 10 years.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Over-triage: the topic words 'bowel cancer screening' match 'Possible malignancy' and 'No change in bowel habit' still matches 'Lower GI red flag' ('no change' is treated as a pseudo-negation). Two priority flags (score 50) → emergency_now for a well 46-year-old. (The negated 'no rectal bleeding' no longer fires.)
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Treat topic words ('cancer screening', a relative's cancer) as context rather than a current malignancy red flag, and treat 'no change in bowel habit' as negated (the matcher currently handles 'no change' as a pseudo-negation).

mustNotAlarm.note: An asymptomatic screening visit must not raise an "emergency now" banner (alarm fatigue; front desk would redirect a well person).
mustNotAlarm.knownGapNote: Web triage raises 'Emergency now — do not auto-book … urgent emergency assessment' for a screening request (see level-routine).
mustNotAlarm.proposedFix: Treat topic words ('cancer screening', a relative's cancer) as context rather than a current malignancy red flag, and treat 'no change in bowel habit' as negated (the matcher currently handles 'no change' as a pseudo-negation).

mustInclude.note: USPSTF 2021 grade B from 45: an average-risk 46-year-old should be offered screening.

mustExclude.note: A screening visit must not generate a cancer staging / resection plan (the working diagnosis contains the words "colorectal cancer").

guideline.name: USPSTF recommendation statement — screening for colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Screen adults 45–49 (grade B) and 50–75 (grade A); 76–85 selectively, considering overall health and prior screening (grade C); stool-based (e.g. annual FIT) or direct visualisation (e.g. colonoscopy every 10 years) strategies
guideline.citation: US Preventive Services Task Force. Screening for colorectal cancer: US Preventive Services Task Force recommendation statement. JAMA. 2021;325:1965–1977.

guideline.name: ACG clinical guidelines — colorectal cancer screening
guideline.section: Average risk: start at 45; one first-degree relative with CRC or advanced adenoma diagnosed < 60, or two FDRs at any age: colonoscopy from 40 (or 10 years before the youngest affected relative) every 5 years
guideline.citation: Shaukat A, Kahi CJ, Burke CA, et al. ACG clinical guidelines: colorectal cancer screening 2021. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:458–479.

rationale: USPSTF 2021 and ACG 2021 lowered the average-risk starting age to 45. The engines should offer FIT or colonoscopy, keep the visit routine, and not treat the words "colorectal cancer screening" as a cancer diagnosis.
